title: Adopt semantic icons where sweeps left stopgaps
goal: A handful of controls in the study borrow an icon that means something else, so the picture does not match what the control does. This gives them icons that actually depict the action, such as left, center and right alignment and horizontal and vertical flip.
notes:
Objective: design-system > icon-conformance (child staged 'later', parent 'design-system' staged 'next'). Focus epic is measure-redline.

VERIFIED 2026-08-24 BEFORE DROPPING - THE PREMISE NO LONGER HOLDS. All three named stopgaps were already replaced by earlier sweeps; there is no work left as written.

Claim by claim, checked against the live files:
  1. "lang-toolbars text-align seg should use alignment icons" - already does. lang-toolbars.html:635 is
     ic-text-align-left / -center / -right. Landed in 3717b7e.
  2. "flip H/V should use flip icons instead of ic-transition" - already does. lang-toolbars.html:486-487
     and :610-611 are ic-flip-horizontal / ic-flip-vertical. Landed in 559a888. No ic-transition anywhere
     is standing in for a flip: all 24 uses across 8 pages mean a real transition (video cross-dissolve),
     a prototype connection, or a motion mapping.
  3. "walkthrough back/next could adopt chevrons" - already does, on all 20 walkthrough pages:
     ic-chevron-left + Back, Next + ic-chevron-right, with no variants. Landed in 559a888.

THE TASK'S OWN SUGGESTION WAS WRONG AND WOULD REGRESS THE PAGE IF RUN LITERALLY. It asked for
ic-align-left/center/right on the TEXT alignment segment. icons.mjs:318 forbids exactly that: "Text-alignment
glyphs are the ragged-line family. Object alignment lives in Transform & arrange and never uses these."
The page already draws the correct distinction. Anyone re-staging this epic should ignore that line of the note.

WIDER SWEEP, since the title is broader than the three spots. Extracted every icon class across all 90 mock
HTML files and resolved each against icons.mjs plus its ALIASES map: 216 known names, ZERO icons used that
are not in the source of truth. Then audited every control whose label or title says align, flip, rotate,
mirror or distribute (35 call sites): object alignment uses ic-align-*, text alignment uses ic-text-align-*,
flips use ic-flip-*, rotation uses ic-rotate-*, distribution uses ic-distribute-*. Every one is semantically
right. The single ic-align-center (alias) use is iconography.html:465, which is the page that documents the
aliases, so it is correct by design.

A label-vs-icon lexical overlap pass flagged 1089 pairs but is not usable evidence: it has no synonym model,
so ic-pen<-"Edit", ic-check<-"Accept", ic-trash<-"Clear All" and ic-plus<-"New conversation" all trip it.
Spot-reading the head of that list found no genuine mismatch. Recording it so nobody re-runs the same
heuristic and mistakes its noise for findings.

NO ICON WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT AS A STAND-IN, so acceptance item 2 has an empty list rather than an unmet one.
acceptance: The text-alignment and flip controls on the toolbar spec page use alignment and flip icons rather than a stand-in
Any icon deliberately left as a stand-in is listed in the task log with the reason
Every touched page loads without error

log.note: import triage: acceptance criteria and deps filled in from study-tasks.json + 2026-08-22 verification
retriage 2026-08-23: notes groomed to name the objective served

Verified before dropping, and the premise does not hold. All three named stopgaps are already fixed in the live files: lang-toolbars.html:635 uses ic-text-align-left/center/right, :486-487 and :610-611 use ic-flip-horizontal/vertical (no ic-transition stand-in anywhere), and all 20 walkthrough pages use ic-chevron-left/right for Back/Next. Wider sweep over all 90 mock HTML files: every icon used resolves to one of the 216 canonical names or aliases in icons.mjs, and all 35 align/flip/rotate/distribute controls carry the semantically correct glyph. Separately, the task's own suggestion was wrong: it asked for ic-align-* on the text-alignment segment, which icons.mjs:318 explicitly forbids, so running it literally would have regressed the page.

Two independent grounds for dropping. (1) Stage gate: this serves design-system > icon-conformance, a child staged 'later' under a parent staged 'next'; the focus epic is measure-redline and only epics staged 'now' may hold open tasks. Same gate that dropped icon-conformance-audit-across-mock-pages, decide-zoom-semantics-on-mock-canvases and show-save-and-dirty-state-across-editor-mocks. (2) The work is already done: every acceptance item passes against the current files without any change from me. No mock files were touched. Full evidence is in notes.
